page: Amazon Web Services m7g.medium is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton3 processors. Built on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture with Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance features 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 2.6 GHz, backed by 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes 4.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Baseline network throughput is configured at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark outcomes show that single-core computational execution delivers mid-range results. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1509.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1406.0, both placing within the average 50% category. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks directly reflect the single vCPU configuration: Geekbench multi-core performance scored 1400.0, and stress-ng multi-core reached 1509.38, ranking in the lower 10%. Memory performance presents 29.56 GB/sec for uncached read-only bandwidth and 10.71 GB/sec for uncached writes, while caching smaller 16 KB blocks hits 96.94 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 1.7 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and 1.94 GB/sec for static web serving.

Given its single dedicated core and baseline resource allocations, the m7g.medium delivers an entry-level compute footprint. It trades aggregated parallel throughput for predictable, dedicated execution on modern Arm silicon. Workload fitness focuses on low-intensity microservices, lightweight web serving, small staging environments, single-threaded batch scripts, and simple internal utility containers.
description: Amazon Web Services m7g.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 Graviton processor running at 2.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 1 dedicated vCPU (1 physical core, 1 thread per core), 4.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage or GPUs. Network bandwidth baseline is 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-core capability, recording 1406.0 in Geekbench and 1509.38 in stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance is limited by the single-core topology, and memory operations achieve 29.56 GB/sec for uncached reads. Redis operations reach 1.7 million operations per second, with static web serving achieving 1.94 GB/sec. This instance serves well for lightweight container hosting, small web services, development environments, and low-traffic backends.
